captions.instagram:
How does a room heater work?

Every electric heater turns 100% of its electricity into heat, yet a halogen warms your face in a second while an oil radiator needs many minutes to get going. Take nine heaters apart in 3D, heat a Delhi bedroom through a January night, and see why an angithi in a closed room can kill.

→ Every electric heater turns all its electricity into heat; they differ in how it reaches you.
→ A halogen heater’s infrared crosses the air and warms you, not the room.
→ Hotter glows brighter: radiated power rises as temperature to the fourth power.
→ An oil radiator stores heat in oil and steel, so it keeps warming after it is switched off.
→ A 2 kW heater warms a Delhi bedroom until its leaks match its power.

youtubeLong.title: How does a room heater work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Every electric heater turns 100% of its electricity into heat, yet a halogen warms your face in a second while an oil radiator needs many minutes to get going. Take nine heaters apart in 3D, heat a Delhi bedroom through a January night, and see why an angithi in a closed room can kill.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/roomheaterclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/roomheaterclear

In this video:
• Every heater is 100% efficient. A heater pushes current through a wire with resistance, and all of that electricity becomes heat: a 2,000 W heater on 230 V mains is about 26 Ω and makes 2 kWh of heat an hour.
• Glow or flow. Radiant heaters (rod, quartz, halogen, carbon) make something glow, and their infrared warms whatever it shines on, in seconds.
• Oil, bimetal and clever stones. An oil-filled radiator stores over 10 kJ per degree in its oil and steel, so it warms slowly and stays warm.
• A room is a leaky box. A typical Indian bedroom leaks about 100 watts for every degree it is held above the outside air.
• Dry air and a silent gas. Warming air adds no water, so humidity falls: foggy 85% outside becomes about 32% indoors at 22 °C.
• Use it safely. Keep a metre clear of curtains and beds, plug a 2 kW heater (8.7 A) into a 16 A wall socket rather than a thin extension board, switch off at bedtime, and buy one with the ISI mark.
